 Coverage by Esteban Monsalve Updated November 9, 2026, 11:27 pm ET ADVERTISEMENT
 Live Last update 11:27 PM ET 11:27 PM ET a minute ago 3Q 6:19: Dejounte Murray has already accumulated one technical foul and one offensive foul
 Dejounte Murray has already accumulated one technical foul and one offensive foul. He has only 6 points, shooting 3-for-7. With such a large deficit, it's understandable that tensions are rising. If he continues to argue in the third quarter, he could be one foul away from ejection.

 Key moments
 11:04 PM ET End of the second quarter 
 10:44 PM ET End of the first quarter 
 10:11 PM ET The match begins 
 Follow VAVEL on Google 11:19 PM ET 10 minutes ago 3Q 8:18: Fears distributes the ball, but he's too isolated
 Fears distributes the ball, but he's too isolated. The Pelicans' point guard has seven assists and is the standout player on offense, though he's only made two of eight shots, a mere 25 percent. He's clearly eager: he's running the team and looking for his teammates. The problem is that many of his passes end in misses, and the visitors' offense just can't seem to get going.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 11:17 PM ET 12 minutes ago 3Q 10:38: A 29-point lead and a home team that was near perfect
 A 29-point lead and a home team that was near perfect in the first half: 12 of 23 from three-point range and only three turnovers. For the Pelicans, who went into halftime shooting just 17.6% from beyond the arc, the goal no longer seems to be winning, but at least putting up a respectable fight. Kerr faces the most delicate task: preventing his team from getting complacent and, at the same time, managing the minutes of his key players.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 11:14 PM ET 15 minutes ago 3Q 12:00: Golden State can afford to rotate their squad and give their key
 With their current lead, Golden State can afford to rotate their squad and give their key players a rest. That's where New Orleans could capitalize and close the gap. If the home team's second unit can maintain their momentum, the game could become difficult for the visitors; if they falter, an opportunity opens up. It remains to be seen whether the Louisiana team can take advantage of that moment or if Kerr can rediscover the winning formula.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 11:04 PM ET 25 minutes ago End of the second quarter
 The second quarter has ended, and therefore, so has the first half of the New Orleans Pelicans vs. Golden State Warriors game. We'll go to halftime, and the game will resume in a few minutes when play restarts.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:58 PM ET 30 minutes ago 2Q 2:10: The Golden State Warriors are finishing the first half with a very
 The Golden State Warriors are finishing the first half with a very positive feeling. This is in stark contrast to the Pelicans, who are plagued by unforced errors and constant turnovers on their inbounds plays.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:53 PM ET 35 minutes ago 2Q 4:18: The visitors are still struggling to string together a scoring run
 The visitors are still struggling to string together a scoring run: their best moment was a run of just 5 points, and so far in the second quarter, they've only managed 2. Dejounte Murray has 4, Derik Queen also has 4 points and two blocks, while Fears has 3 points and 4 assists. There are flashes of brilliance, but no one has quite taken control. With only 22 points, the Pelicans need to find their rhythm soon, or the game could be over before halftime.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:53 PM ET 36 minutes ago 2Q 6:03: The Golden State Warriors' lead is now double that of the New Orleans Pelicans
 The Golden State Warriors' lead is now double that of the New Orleans Pelicans. The difference is significant for only being in the second quarter. The visitors' lack of efficiency has taken its toll, and it shows on the scoreboard.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:51 PM ET 37 minutes ago 2Q 8:43: Al Horford scores two points for the Golden State Warriors
 Al Horford scores two points for the Golden State Warriors after a play by Draymond Green, who provided the assist with a beautiful through ball. The home team's lead over the New OrleansPelicans continues.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:47 PM ET 41 minutes ago 2Q 10:45: The three-pointers aren't working for New Orleans
 The three-pointers aren't working for New Orleans. They've only made two of their twelve attempts, a mere 16.7 percent, and that statistic helps explain a good part of the score. The Louisiana team is finding shots in the paint and converting them, but when they spread out to shoot from deep, the ball just won't fall. Between Fears, Mathurin, Murray, and company, there are more misses than hits, and every three-pointer that bounces off the rim only widens the gap.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:44 PM ET 44 minutes ago End of the first quarter
 Golden State closes the quarter with a 15-point lead and the impression of having been comfortable from the start. The Pelicans are held to 20 points, their offense stalling every time they had to attempt a long-range shot. The home team simply moved the ball quickly to repeatedly find an open teammate. The deficit is still within reach, but the task becomes more difficult if New Orleans doesn't improve their shooting and perimeter defense.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:28 PM ET an hour ago 1Q 1:03: Brandon Williams scores a layup after receiving an assist from Brandin Podziemski
 Brandon Williams scores a layup after receiving an assist from Brandin Podziemski. Williams gained confidence and, with a driving drive, went up to the basket and added two more points for the San Francisco team.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:26 PM ET an hour ago 1Q 3:51: Curry hasn't been very effective at the start of the game
 Curry hasn't been very effective at the start of the game. He's already missed three shots, although he does have eight points so far in the first quarter. The New Orleans Pelicans are gaining confidence.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:24 PM ET an hour ago 1Q 5:17: Interestingly, there aren't many three-point attempts, and the teams
 Interestingly, there aren't many three-point attempts, and the teams are quite conservative. They prefer to drive to the basket and secure the layup to avoid giving the opponent an advantage with a turnover.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:20 PM ET an hour ago 1Q 7:28: The Golden State Warriors' lead over the New Orleans Pelicans has increased
 The Golden State Warriors' lead over the New Orleans Pelicans has increased to seven points, and a slight shift in the game is becoming noticeable. San Francisco is being more persistent with their pressure and accuracy. New Orleans has missed a couple of shots.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:18 PM ET an hour ago 1Q 9:02: Dejounte Murray commits a personal foul on an opponent's shot
 Dejounte Murray commits a personal foul on an opponent's shot. It will be a free throw for the Golden State Warriors, who are comfortably leading the game with a strong start. There's still plenty of time left to play.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:16 PM ET an hour ago 1Q 11:37: Stephen Curry scores a layup early, giving the Warriors the lead
 Stephen Curry scores a layup early, giving the Warriors the lead. The home team is using possession and efficiency as a weapon, and it's clear they know how to use it. They're currently winning by five points.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:11 PM ET an hour ago The match begins
 The ball is tipped off and the NBA game between the New Orleans Pelicans and the Golden State Warriors officially begins, live on VAVEL.com.
 The Warriors have the first possession and the action kicks off.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:08 PM ET an hour ago One year difference
 The best way to gauge the gap between the two franchises is to compare them to their standings twelve months ago. Golden State finished last season with a 37-45 record; they are now 7-3. New Orleans, which finished with a 26-56 record, fired Willie Green on November 15, 2025, after starting the season 2-10. At this same time last year, they were 2-12. Today they are 4-6: a tangible improvement, though still insufficient. Betting odds from specialized media outlets have the score between 125-113 and 116-110 in favor of the Warriors. Almost no one expects a Pelicans victory, although several recommend betting on the visiting team to cover the 9.5-point deficit.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:07 PM ET an hour ago The weight of historical statistics
 The Warriors have won 19 of their last 20 home games against the Pelicans after coming off a win, and they return to the court after Saturday's overtime victory. However, one statistic works against them: they've lost their last four home games against Southwest Division teams. New Orleans, on the other hand, has won five of its last six back-to-back games after being the underdog, so the outcome shouldn't be taken for granted. The last meeting between the two was on February 24 in New Orleans, and it ended 113-109.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:06 PM ET an hour ago The line that resists
 There's an interesting detail in how the market has evolved throughout the day: the spread opened with Golden State favored by 9.5 points, dropped to 8.5 twice, and then returned to 9.5 before tip-off. The odds for a Warriors win range from -375 to -450, while a New Orleans victory pays between +300 and +350. The total points are currently between 231.5 and 232.5.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:05 PM ET an hour ago Where can the night go wrong?
 New Orleans has a chance to stay in the game. If Fears and Murray attack the basket decisively, Matkovic takes advantage of Missi's absence to dominate in the paint, and Golden State relaxes with their lead, the score could remain close until the end. Even so, it's more likely that Curry and Lendeborg will set the pace, that fatigue will take its toll on a team with three starters out, and that the difference from beyond the arc will ultimately tip the scales. The teams will face off again on Monday the 16th, at 8:00 p.m., at the Smoothie King Center in New Orleans; therefore, tonight's game also serves as the first round.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:04 PM ET an hour ago A start that went awry and then straightened out
 Looking at New Orleans' schedule, it reads like the story of a team torn in two. The season began with four straight losses: by three points to Indiana, by one in Utah, by six in overtime in Denver, and by 13 at home, also against Denver. Then came four consecutive wins: against Sacramento, a comfortable 121-99 victory against Atlanta, a close 135-134 win in Memphis, and a 120-113 win against Utah. But just when it seemed the team was starting to get back on track, they fell at home to Minnesota 115-109 and yesterday lost 139-123 against the Clippers. Those 139 points are the second-highest total New Orleans has allowed this season; the only worse was Denver's 141.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:03 PM ET an hour ago Any alternatives for the visit?
 Zion's absence is compounded by those of Trey Murphy III, who is suffering from patellar tendinopathy in both knees; Yves Missi, with a bone contusion in his left knee; and Trendon Watford, who is nursing a sprained right ankle. In other words, two of the team's four leading scorers will be unavailable. With so many absences, the starting lineup will most likely consist of Jeremiah Fears, Dejounte Murray, and Karlo Matkovic, along with two of these three: Saddiq Bey, Herbert Jones, and Benedict Mathurin, who will compete for the minutes left by Murphy.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:02 PM ET an hour ago Pelicans, fatigue, and Zion's night off
 The big news ahead of the game is an absence, as Zion Williamson will miss his first game of the season for rest, since it's the second night of a back-to-back. He had played in all 10 games this year, averaging 21 points, 5.3 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 2.2 steals. Last night, against the Clippers, he was flawless: he made all nine of his shots and scored 25 points. The decision is to protect him, not due to injury, although in New Orleans, injuries are among the most debated, given his history of physical problems. In seven seasons, Zion has missed 278 games, including an entire season.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:01 PM ET an hour ago The Warriors' infirmary, again
 The Golden State Warriors' injury list continues to grow: Will Richard, who had been a starter in recent weeks, was added to the list this week with a torn ulnar collateral ligament in his left thumb. Jimmy Butler is still recovering from the ACL surgery he underwent in January. Moses Moody is still dealing with a patellar tendon injury, while Kristaps Porziņģis is listed as out and reportedly staying away from the team and basketball for health reasons. Gui Santos is listed as probable despite tendinitis in his left knee, and Gary Payton II is questionable.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 10:00 PM ET an hour ago The homeowners' amulet
 Curry is averaging 31.3 points per game, the second-best mark in the league. The last time he averaged over 30 points in a season was in 2020-21, when he finished with 32. But Golden State doesn't rely solely on him. Rookie Yaxel Lendeborg tallied 23 points, eight rebounds, three assists, and three blocks against the Magic, and is already averaging 21.2 points and 7.2 rebounds. Brandin Podziemski is contributing 15.8 points per night, shooting 47.4% from the field and 39.2% from three-point range, while Draymond Green continues to anchor the defense. The Warriors lead the NBA in three-point percentage, rank fifth in offense, and 14th in defense: they win more thanks to their shooting than their ability to protect the rim.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 9:59 PM ET an hour ago Warriors: Curry, overtime, and a long weekend
 Last Saturday's game deserves its own paragraph. Golden State defeated Orlando 124-119 in overtime, with Stephen Curry leading the charge: he tallied 41 points, six rebounds, and six assists, scoring 19 points between the fourth quarter and overtime. His four field goals in the final period either tied the game or gave his team the lead in the last three minutes. He also reached 100 consecutive games with at least one three-pointer, a streak he had already achieved twice before in his career.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 9:56 PM ET 2 hours ago Welcome
 Welcome to our live coverage of the New Orleans Pelicans vs. Golden State Warriors game, part of the 2026-27 NBA regular season. We'll begin with the pre-game showdown.
 Who will win this NBA regular season matchup?
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 9:54 PM ET 2 hours ago Preview
 In the NBA, there are nights when the numbers matter more than the plays themselves. The Warriors come into this game riding a seven-game winning streak and riding high. The Pelicans, on the other hand, have a 4-6 record, are coming off a loss last night in Los Angeles, and are facing the second night of a back-to-back with half their roster out. Models give Golden State an 83% chance of winning, while various media outlets are predicting scores like 125-113 or 124-108.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 9:54 PM ET 2 hours ago The Warriors' last five games
 In their most recent victory, they defeated the Orlando Magic 126-119. They have won five of their last five games. During that stretch, they scored 598 points, averaging 119.6 per game, and allowed 539 (107.8 per game), for an average point differential of +11.8. Their closest win was by three points against Phoenix, and their largest by 20 against Miami.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 9:54 PM ET 2 hours ago The Pelicans' last five games
 Their record is four wins and one loss. In those five games, they scored 617 points, averaging 123.4 per game, and allowed 581, or 116.2 per game. Four games were at home; their only away game was against Memphis, which they won by one point. This explains the 4-5 record I mentioned earlier: if they managed four wins in their last five games, they started the season with four consecutive losses.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 9:29 PM ET 2 hours ago There is one point in common
 Although it might not seem like it at first glance, both teams have something in common: they struggle to defend their own half. This suggests a high-scoring game. The difference lies in their approach: Golden State moves the ball better and is coming off a comfortable win, while New Orleans is coming off a close loss but boasts an offense that has scored over 120 points.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 8:52 PM ET 3 hours ago It could be a great game
 Everything points to a high-scoring game with few interruptions. One statistic worth noting is that the Pelicans are shooting just 32.7% from three-point range, while the Warriors are holding them to nearly 34.5%, thanks to Curry's efficiency.
 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 8:17 PM ET 3 hours ago The clash of styles
 New Orleans averages 120.2 points per game, the third-highest mark in the league, but also allows 118.8. This combination places them among the weakest defensive teams: they score a lot, but struggle to contain their opponents. Golden State, on the other hand, plays a more collective and balanced style of basketball. Even so, they aren't known for their defensive solidity either: their opponents shoot 47.5% from the field, which leaves certain aspects of their offense to chance.

 Live updates by Esteban Monsalve
 7:15 PM ET 4 hours ago Chase Center
 The Chase Center is the arena in San Francisco, California, where basketball games and shows are held. It is also the home of the NBA's Golden State Warriors. Located in Mission Bay, by the bay, at 1 Warriors Way, near the intersection of Third and 16th Streets, its rounded exterior, white facades, and large windows make it instantly recognizable. Modern office towers and laboratories rise behind it. The arena is part of a larger complex that includes offices, shops, restaurants, and a plaza.
 To understand its origins, one must go back to the history of the Warriors. The team was founded in Philadelphia in 1946 and arrived in the San Francisco Bay Area in 1962. From 1971, they played in the Oakland arena, which for many years was called Oracle Arena. They only moved from there briefly: in the 1996-97 season, they played in San Jose while the arena was being renovated. Oracle Arena, with a capacity of nearly 19,600, was the oldest arena in the NBA. Over time, it became outdated, and management began considering a return to San Francisco. The move was announced in 2012, and construction on the Chase Center began on January 17, 2017.
 The Chase Center seats 18,064 basketball players, slightly less than Oracle Arena, and around 19,500 concertgoers. It also features 44 suites in the upper deck, 32 courtside lounges, and 60 theater-style suites. The arena also offers several dining and beverage options.

 7:15 PM ET 4 hours ago How the two teams are doing
 Golden State has a 6-3 record, while New Orleans is 4-5. The Warriors are coming off a comfortable 120-100 victory over Miami. Stephen Curry scored 29 points in just 28 minutes, and the team shot 52.5% from the field. The Pelicans, meanwhile, lost 115-109 to Minnesota, despite Jeremiah Fears' 24 points in 36 minutes.
